enhanced.fullText:
The Age Discrimination Act of 1975, codified at 42 U.S.C. §§ 6101-6107, prohibits discrimination based on age in programs or activities receiving federal financial assistance, including higher education institutions. This comprehensive civil rights law extends beyond employment to encompass all educational services, academic programs, and institutional activities funded by federal agencies.

Under 42 U.S.C. § 6102, institutions must ensure that no person shall, on the basis of age, be excluded from participation in, denied benefits of, or subjected to discrimination under any program or activity receiving federal financial assistance. The Department of Health and Human Services regulations at 45 CFR Part 90 establish specific compliance standards for educational institutions.

Higher education institutions must maintain non-discriminatory policies in admissions, academic programs, student services, financial aid, and extracurricular activities. The Act permits age distinctions only when they constitute a normal or statutory requirement for participation or when the federal agency providing assistance establishes that age is a reasonable factor necessary to achieve program objectives, as specified in 42 U.S.C. § 6103(b).

Enforcement mechanisms include complaint investigations by the Office for Civil Rights (OCR), compliance reviews, and potential termination of federal funding under 42 U.S.C. § 6104. Institutions face administrative enforcement through fund suspension or termination procedures, following the same processes established under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. Individual complainants may file administrative complaints with OCR within 180 days of alleged discrimination.

The Act's anti-retaliation provisions under 42 U.S.C. § 6102 protect individuals who file complaints, participate in investigations, or advocate for rights protected by the statute. Retaliation includes any adverse action taken because of protected activity, encompassing academic sanctions, denial of services, or harassment.

Recent regulatory guidance emphasizes proactive compliance through policy development, staff training, and grievance procedures. Institutions must designate responsible officials, establish internal complaint processes, and maintain documentation of compliance efforts. The 2020 amendments to enforcement procedures require enhanced coordination between federal agencies and standardized investigation protocols under Executive Order 12250.
enhanced.summary: The Age Discrimination Act of 1975 (42 U.S.C. §§ 6101-6107) prohibits age-based discrimination in federally-funded educational programs. Universities must ensure equal access to academic programs, services, and activities regardless of age, with limited exceptions for reasonable program requirements.
enhanced.requirements:
## Core Anti-Discrimination Obligations
- Prohibit age discrimination in all federally-funded programs and activities per 42 U.S.C. § 6102
- Ensure equal access to admissions, academic programs, student services, and financial aid
- Implement reasonable accommodations for age-related needs in educational delivery
- Maintain written non-discrimination policies covering all institutional operations

## Policy and Procedural Requirements
- Designate responsible compliance officers for Age Discrimination Act oversight
- Establish internal grievance procedures for age discrimination complaints
- Provide annual training for faculty and staff on age discrimination prevention
- Conduct periodic reviews of policies and practices for discriminatory impact

## Anti-Retaliation Protections
- Prohibit retaliation against individuals filing complaints or participating in investigations
- Monitor for adverse actions following protected activity under 42 U.S.C. § 6102
- Document and investigate all retaliation allegations promptly and thoroughly
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No routine reporting required to federal agencies. Institutions must respond to OCR complaints within 30 days and compliance reviews within specified timeframes. Maintain internal documentation of discrimination complaints and resolutions for potential federal review.
